findings.body: The previously reported signed-commit defect remains: with log.showSignature=true, this git show can include signature information alongside the tree hash. repo.git returns the entire trimmed stdout (src/forge/repo.py:144), which is then embedded into diff-tree --stdin as a tree ID. That invalid input breaks both JSON commands and the human board because they share _copies. Read the tree with rev-parse <ref>^{tree}, or explicitly disable signature output.
findings.title: Disable signature output when reading the landed tree ID

findings.body: The previously reported restart defect remains: dates contains historical additions even when their state files have been removed from the landed tree, and this comprehension expires those paths unconditionally. After reverting an old fix merge and deleting its refs, fix_start permits the same slug because its state is absent (src/forge/task.py:273). The new ongoing fix is then hidden by both JSON commands, and next skips its guidance. Restarted tasks have the same problem. Require the path to exist in landed_states before treating its historical addition date as a current merge.
findings.title: Do not expire restarted tasks and fixes using reverted merge dates

why: forge board --json takes about 45 seconds and forge next --json about 10, so the pane's 10-second refresh would keep a core busy in every open Claude Code session
